subject: general
question: After the end of industrial licensing in India in 1991, ________ is one of the few industries for which it is mandatory to obtain an industrial license.
solution:
The correct answer is__** Liquor.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the 1991 policy, except for 18 major industries, all other industries were exempted from licensing, which reduced the number of industries to 5 due to the need for licensing.
 
• Industries for which a license is now mandatory
 
 
• **distillation of alcoholic beverages**
 
• **Cigar cigarettes of tobacco and other alternatives to regulated tobacco**
 
• **Electronic Aerospace & Security Equipment**
 
• **Industrial Explosives - Industrial explosives including detonative fuses, safety fuses, gun-powder, nitrocellulose and matches**
 
• **Hazardous Chemicals**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****India's 1991 Industrial Policy**

 
• **New Industrial Policy 1991 was announced in 1991 in the Lok Sabha on July 24, 1991.**
 
• This policy was **announced by the Minister of State for Industry, P.J. Made by Thungan.**
 
• Prior to the new industrial policy, prior permission of the Government of India was mandatory before foreign investment in India or bringing new (foreign) technology into India.
 
• Government interference and the approval process were creating unwanted delays in business decisions.
 
• In the new industrial policy, a list of priority industries related to high-tech and high investment was made, in which FDI up to 51 per cent was automatically allowed.
 
• Under the new industrial policy, the requirement of obtaining permission from the central government before setting up industries in cities with a population of less than 10 lakhs has been dispensed with.
